sermon.title: The Helpers and the Helped
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 31 and 32: those who rely on human help instead of God, and those who help them, fall together. He says trust in leaders, armies, ourselves and religion must be restricted, then reads the lion and shepherds allegory, and calls believers to speak and reign in righteousness.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: the captions garble a few words and these are marked [unclear] (about 21:15, 22:05, 23:15 and 41:00). He reads “Isaiah 31:1” as “31 1” and gives “Isaiah 37 31:7” in the captions for Isaiah 31:7; “Isaiah 5611” is Isaiah 56:11; “Revelations 1:” is written Revelation 1:5-6; and “2 Kings 1, I mean, Isaiah 32:1” is his own correction. “Jehosaphat” is written Jehoshaphat. He quotes the “Jeremiah 7” passage on lying words without giving the reference. In the passage about “Philippians 3” he says “Paul said this” without naming the book. This is a sensitive message: he calls humanists “atheists… homosexual activists… communists… socialists” (about 4:00), says “our civil government says homosexuals were born that way” (about 11:35), says “our government lies to us all the time” (about 12:20), names a well-known pastor and author as a leader of a social-reform movement (about 16:45), mentions “women’s health… birth control… an abortion” (about 19:10), says people will die Baptist or Catholic (about 14:35), says “we don’t need a Pope” (about 28:05), refers to a popular prophecy book “by a Jewish rabbi” and to 9/11 and a stock market fall as read into Jeremiah (about 32:15), and uses the word “Eskimo.” The caption says “5% of Christians now go to a home church” and he gives 185,000 as the number in Isaiah 37:36; these are as spoken. He also mentions a basketball and a boxing match without naming them.

chunks.section_question: What does Isaiah 32 promise when the Spirit is poured out? (Isaiah 32:3-4)
chunks.short_answer: He reads “The tongue of stammerers will be ready to speak plainly,” and says “pick up the pace.” He says “the foolish will continue to speak foolishness,” and that when the Spirit is poured out, “the wilderness becomes a fruitful field.”
chunks.text:
Lord, that day that we return to the God, we turn back to God, we put our trust in Jesus. Isaiah 32:3: “The eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, the ears of those who hear will continually listen, the heart of the hasty will understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.” Those of you who’ve been lazy in reading your Bible, lazy in studying, lazy in going to Bible studies, pick up the pace. Because it’s the quick, it’s the ones that get out there and run the race that will get the knowledge and understanding. Amen. Amen. Pick up the pace. Say it: pick up the pace. It’s not for the lazy. A lot of us don’t know anything because we’re just flat-out lazy. We’ve got a zillion excuses why we can’t find time to read that book, go to a Bible study, and learn the Word. Am I right? Yeah.

“And the tongue of the stammerers.” How, you had a hard time witnessing to people, [unclear] to your teeth. You know, when people ask you a question in the Bible, “Pastor Dave, come over here.” Ain’t I right? Yeah. [unclear] stammerer, but he says “in that day that we turn we will be ready to speak,” and he has an adjective in there, “plainly,” clearly. We make sense because we’ve got something to say. How many know if you don’t have anything to say, you can’t talk? Oh, that’s not true. In America, we talk whether we’ve got anything to say or not. We just act like we know the Bible whether we know it or

not. Isn’t this a tremendous promise that Isaiah has given us? And people want to buy high-banger books and Late Great Planet Earth books, and Isaiah’s there just filled with juicy stuff. But “the foolish will continue to speak foolishness, they will work iniquity, lawlessness, they’ll practice ungodliness, they’ll utter error against the Lord.” Why? Because they’re getting help from the secular, from the human side, and they don’t trust in nor seek the Lord, so they just continue sinning, they just continue being fools. Remember Jesus said that the people at the flood did not know until the flood came and took them away. So shall it be in the second coming. There will be people on earth no matter how great God moves before He comes, and we see there is something tremendous in the future here that God’s going to demonstrate Himself. There’s still going to be people who refuse to listen, and they’re not going to know till Jesus pops through the sky and it’s too late. And people say, “How can that be if He really demonstrates Himself?” Well, He was here 2,000 years ago, and they rejected Him.

Are you there? Hallelujah. In the wilderness, He did all those judgments, and Egypt still wouldn’t believe. And then Isaiah 32:4, “until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high.” I love the prayer time today focusing on the Holy Spirit. “Until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high, the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is counted as a forest, with justice and righteousness.” So here is a visitation of Bible morality and a fruitful field. You know, we can have a 10-acre field, but you know, you don’t have a 10-acre

forest. A forest is something that spreads over the country, miles and miles, trees after trees after trees. So this is going to be a visitation of Bible morality, and it’s going to go from the field, which is His church, and just spread. The Bible says we’re called “trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord.” Amen. We’re His orchard. We need leaders. God chooses humans to work with, but we are restricted. If we don’t get a hold of this Man Jesus and His Word, we are restricted in how effective we can be.

faqs.question: What does he say humanists believe about the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “humanists reject the Bible. It’s not the Word of God, it has a lot of errors in it.” He answers, “The Bible says as the Spirit inspired them, they wrote. That’s a big difference.”

faqs.question: What does he say happens to the helper and the helped?
faqs.answer: He says “here they all, all,” being the helper and the helped, “will perish together,” and “we can’t plead ignorance.”

faqs.question: Can we trust armies and rulers?
faqs.answer: He says “we need armies to protect our families,” but “we need to restrict our trust in them,” and “we need rulers… but you’ve got to restrict your trust in them because they are human beings.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will remember the name of the LORD our God.

faqs.question: How much should we trust ourselves?

faqs.question: What is the difference between a believer and a disciple?
faqs.answer: He says “a disciple is an obedient one, not a believer,” and “they’re responsible to the Word of God to obey it. They fail, they get up, they admit they’re wrong, they get up and they keep going.”

faqs.question: What does the young lion represent?
faqs.answer: He says of Hosea 5:14, “I will be a young lion to Judah. That’s Jesus talking, the Lord talking.” He says “I told you the Bible explains itself.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the title “pastor”?
faqs.answer: He says “putting a title on you as a pastor, that means nothing. Pastor is a job description.”

faqs.question: Does he say believers need a human priest?
faqs.answer: He says “we’re all priests that can go in before God… We can go in Christ ourselves, we can hear from Him, and we can come out and we can be a blessing to others.”

faqs.question: Why does he say believers must speak?
faqs.answer: He says “if you’re silent when you go out these doors, you’re not helping anybody,” and “Jesus was on earth for 30 years and never did anything, had no effect on the world, none, until He started speaking.”

faqs.question: Does he say America is special to God?
faqs.answer: He says “America is no special child of God,” and “God loves the whole world.”

faqs.question: How does he say Assyria fell?
faqs.answer: He says “Assyria shall fall by the sword, not of man,” and “185,000 died in one night of the Assyrian army. 185,000 by the sword of the angel.”
